findings: Neet retains a full narrow tan torso, four separately traceable fine legs with floor contact, broad triangular ears, projecting muzzle and tiny nub. The Dane towers over him without shrinking his body into an unsupported head-and-legs shape.

Buddy sits on the bench beside the closed cat carrier; his torso joins neck and folded hindquarters, and both forepaws plus folded rear supports sit on the cushion. Pale muzzle, brows, pendant ears and distal paws distinguish him from the other dogs.
Torso fills are smooth broad shades; paper grain does not become raised curls, engraved strand patterns or enlarged short-coat volume. Furnished edges remain regional around Buddy face and ears.

The Dane looks weary while Neet looks admiring and Buddy anxious, making the sock misunderstanding readable. No visible sock or tooth prematurely resolves the scene. Vet bench, carrier, door and floor perspective are coherent.

Buddy has a continuous moderately elongated torso with deep chest and real clearance. Four substantial legs trace to shoulder or pelvis and four paws carry weight on the floor; neck and backward head turn remain connected.

His short dark flank is rendered in restrained washes, with a clean back contour. Pale beard, brows, ear fringe and paw tips retain regional grooming; the light chest is predominantly color rather than a shaggy body mass.
Neet is separately seated behind with both forepaws lowered, broad ears, slim forelegs and supported hindquarters. Buddy looking back at him gives the toy-ownership reversal a clear visual target.

The cropped scrub-clad technician is provisional human appearance. Heather is absent, no chew toy has been invented in the room, and clinic furnishings remain consistent with the preceding scene. Floor contact and spatial depth read coherently.

Buddy reclines with a continuous elongated ribcage-to-pelvis silhouette. His folded rear limb joins the pelvis, near foreleg rests on the table, and raised forepaw joins a bent forelimb whose elbow is supported. No detached or shared limbs are visible.

Head size, projecting cream muzzle, light brows and hanging furnished ears preserve Buddy identity. Dark torso mottling reads as subdued watercolor granulation, without a curled fur ridge or enlarged shaggy flank silhouette. Face, ear and foot furnishings remain distinct.

The padded table visibly supports Buddy chest, belly and haunch; its pedestal and base support the load. Nurse dog and terrier have independent floor positions and remain separated from Buddy anatomy.

Raised paw and dopey expression match the anesthesia conversation before the gold-tooth suggestion. Nurse cap, laughing scruffy terrier, clinic equipment and wavy frame identify the dream; no gold tooth or literal gravy boat spoils the subsequent lines. The nurse is a somewhat fluffy provisional Labrador interpretation, a minor supporting-character styling issue rather than a Buddy identity defect.
